title: The Death Files
subtitle: Who died. What they knew. Who they knew. What changed.
boundary: Inclusion does not imply murder, conspiracy, or wrongdoing by any connected person. Official findings, established evidence, disputed claims, analytical inference, and speculation are displayed separately.

dossiers.name: John F. Kennedy
dossiers.caseStatus: Officially resolved; historical findings and records remain actively examined
dossiers.whyMatters: Kennedy's assassination changed presidential security, national politics, Cold War history, public trust, and the architecture of government secrecy. The official record continues to expand through document releases.
dossiers.cinematicOpening: At 12:30 p.m. on November 22, 1963, the presidential motorcade entered Dealey Plaza. Within minutes, President John F. Kennedy had been fatally wounded and Dallas had become the centre of an investigation that would outlive nearly everyone present.
dossiers.officialAccount: The Warren Commission concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald fired the shots and acted alone. The later House Select Committee on Assassinations agreed that Oswald fired the shots but criticised aspects of the earlier investigation and concluded that Kennedy was probably assassinated as a result of a conspiracy; it did not identify another gunman or the scope of a conspiracy.
dossiers.evidenceConclusion: The record strongly supports that Kennedy was killed by gunfire in Dealey Plaza and that Oswald was central to the crime. Disagreement persists over whether all relevant actors, intelligence, and institutional failures were fully identified. New releases must be assessed document by document.
dossiers.analyticalInference: The gap between a formally resolved homicide and a still-expanding official archive justifies continuing records analysis, but it does not itself prove a hidden operational sponsor.
dossiers.speculation: Alternative-gunman, intelligence-operation, organised-crime, anti-Castro, pro-Castro, and institutional-cover-up theories must each be tested against authenticated records, ballistics, timelines, witness reliability, provenance, and counter-evidence.

involvements.label: Cold War executive power
involvements.detail: Kennedy held ultimate executive authority during major Cold War confrontations.

involvements.label: National-security oversight
involvements.detail: His office directed and interacted with the CIA, FBI, Department of Defense, and State Department.

knowledge.label: Classified national-security information
knowledge.detail: The presidency gave Kennedy access to the highest levels of United States national-security information.

knowledge.label: A specific secret as the murder motive
knowledge.detail: Such a claim requires evidence connecting knowledge, motive, capability, and action.

relationships.name: Lee Harvey Oswald
relationships.boundary: Oswald was killed before trial; the evidence was assessed by official inquiries rather than a criminal jury.

relationships.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
relationships.boundary: Succession is a constitutional consequence and is not evidence of involvement.

relationships.name: United States Secret Service
relationships.boundary: Protection failures do not themselves establish conspiracy.

timeline.event: Kennedy was shot while travelling through Dealey Plaza.
Kennedy was pronounced dead at Parkland Memorial Hospital.
The Warren Commission delivered its report.
The House Select Committee on Assassinations issued its report.
The National Archives began a major new release of previously withheld classified records.
The National Archives added a further digitised release.

questions.needed: Theory-by-theory testing rather than cumulative suspicion.

Congress created a statutory disclosure regime for assassination records.

money.detail: Executive authority transferred immediately to the vice president.

money.label: Benefit as proof of responsibility
money.detail: Political or institutional benefit is not evidence of participation in a death.

dossiers.name: Diana, Princess of Wales
dossiers.occupation: Member of the British royal family and humanitarian campaigner
dossiers.officialCause: Injuries sustained in a motor-vehicle collision
dossiers.officialManner: Unlawful killing conclusion at the British inquest, attributed to grossly negligent driving by the driver and pursuing paparazzi vehicles
dossiers.caseStatus: Inquests concluded; extensive evidence archive preserved
dossiers.whyMatters: Diana's death transformed debate about press intrusion, royal institutions, road safety, emergency response, and the treatment of public figures.
dossiers.cinematicOpening: In the early hours of August 31, 1997, a Mercedes carrying Diana, Dodi Fayed, Henri Paul, and Trevor Rees-Jones entered the Pont de l'Alma underpass in Paris. The collision became a global event before the evidence had been fully examined.
dossiers.officialAccount: French and British investigations concluded that the crash was caused principally by Henri Paul's impaired and excessive-speed driving, with pursuing paparazzi vehicles also part of the circumstances considered by the British inquest. The jury returned an unlawful-killing conclusion based on grossly negligent driving.
dossiers.evidenceConclusion: The strongest official evidence supports a fatal high-speed collision involving impaired and grossly negligent driving, compounded by the pursuit environment and failure to wear seatbelts. A planned-assassination claim requires stronger evidence than anomaly aggregation.
dossiers.analyticalInference: Media pressure, security decisions, relationships, and official institutions converged in a short final timeline. That convergence warrants reconstruction but is not proof of coordination.
dossiers.speculation: Assassination, intelligence-service, vehicle-interference, medical-treatment, and pregnancy theories must be separated into testable claims and compared against the inquest record and forensic evidence.

involvements.label: Humanitarian campaigning
involvements.detail: Diana supported landmine clearance and HIV/AIDS awareness.

involvements.label: Global media scrutiny
involvements.detail: Her private life and movements were subject to exceptional press attention.

knowledge.label: Royal household experience
knowledge.detail: Her former position gave her direct experience of royal and state-linked institutions.

knowledge.label: Secret knowledge as motive
knowledge.detail: No alleged secret should be treated as motive without authenticated records.

relationships.name: Dodi Fayed
relationships.boundary: Relevant to the final timeline and travel arrangements.

relationships.name: Henri Paul
relationships.boundary: Official findings attributed grossly negligent driving to him; he also died.

relationships.name: Trevor Rees-Jones
relationships.boundary: His injuries affected his memory of the event.

timeline.event: Diana and Dodi Fayed were at the Ritz Hotel before departing by car.
The Mercedes crashed in the Pont de l'Alma underpass.
The Metropolitan Police began Operation Paget.
The inquest jury returned an unlawful-killing conclusion.

questions.question: Which recurring claims are contradicted by the inquest evidence database?
questions.needed: Claim-level comparison with transcripts and exhibits.

questions.question: What role did media pursuit and security decisions play in the risk chain?
questions.needed: Integrated route, vehicle, speed, impairment, and seatbelt timeline.

aftermath: Public mourning altered the relationship between monarchy, media, and public.
Press and paparazzi practices faced renewed scrutiny.

money.label: Estate and succession
money.detail: Inheritance consequences followed the death but do not establish causation.

money.label: Media economic incentives
money.detail: Demand for exclusive images formed part of the pursuit environment; it does not prove a planned killing.

dossiers.name: Jeffrey Epstein
dossiers.place: Metropolitan Correctional Center, New York City, United States
dossiers.caseStatus: Death investigation concluded; related records, litigation, and disclosures continue
investigatingAuthorities: New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner
U.S. Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General
dossiers.whyMatters: Epstein died while awaiting federal prosecution, ending the criminal case against him personally and intensifying scrutiny of associates, finances, the estate, custodial treatment, and institutional failures.
dossiers.cinematicOpening: At approximately 6:30 a.m. on August 10, 2019, staff at the Metropolitan Correctional Center found Jeffrey Epstein unresponsive in his locked cell. He had been left alone and unmonitored for hours despite recent suicide-watch history.
dossiers.officialAccount: The New York City medical examiner ruled the death a suicide by hanging. The DOJ Inspector General documented numerous serious prison failures and reported that it found no evidence contradicting the FBI's determination that there was no criminality associated with the death.
dossiers.evidenceConclusion: The strongest official evidence supports suicide in a setting of severe and documented custodial failure. Those failures created legitimate suspicion and require accountability, but operational failure is not proof of homicide.
dossiers.analyticalInference: The prison system failed to preserve both a detainee's life and the public's opportunity for a full criminal trial. That institutional failure had consequences independent of any broader theory.
dossiers.speculation: Homicide, assisted-suicide, intelligence-protection, blackmail-network, and evidence-suppression theories require a direct evidentiary chain and cannot be inferred solely from Epstein's connections or the scale of prison failures.

involvements.label: Federal sex-trafficking prosecution
involvements.detail: Epstein was detained pending trial on federal charges.

involvements.label: Network of wealthy and influential contacts
involvements.detail: Relationships are documented, but association does not establish criminal knowledge or conduct.

involvements.label: Estate and civil litigation
involvements.detail: His death shifted accountability efforts toward the estate, institutions, and related proceedings.

knowledge.label: His own conduct, finances, and relationships
knowledge.detail: Epstein possessed direct knowledge of his own activities and relationships.

knowledge.label: A comprehensive blackmail archive
knowledge.detail: This requires authenticated evidence, provenance, and proof of intended use.

relationships.name: Federal Bureau of Prisons
relationships.boundary: The OIG documented serious failures; failure is not proof of homicide.

relationships.name: Ghislaine Maxwell
relationships.type: Long-term associate later convicted in a related federal case
relationships.boundary: The relationship is central to the wider criminal history but is not evidence of involvement in the death.

relationships.name: Named social and professional contacts
relationships.boundary: A contact entry, photograph, flight record, or email does not establish participation in abuse or the death.

timeline.event: Epstein was arrested on federal sex-trafficking charges.
The OIG timeline placed the start of an extended period in which Epstein was alone and unmonitored.
Epstein was discovered hanging in his locked cell.
The DOJ Inspector General released its custody and supervision report.
The DOJ announced publication of millions of additional responsive pages.

questions.question: Do later releases contain evidence that changes the death assessment?
questions.needed: Authenticated material tied to the death investigation and compared with the OIG record.

questions.question: How did multiple safeguards fail during the final night?
questions.needed: Staffing, rounds, cell assignment, linen, camera, access, and supervision viewed as one system.

aftermath: The federal criminal prosecution against Epstein personally ended.
Victims pursued compensation and accountability through the estate and civil litigation.
The DOJ OIG issued eight institutional recommendations.
The DOJ Epstein Library continued to expand through July 2026.

money.label: Estate administration and victim compensation
money.detail: The estate became a central route for compensation, litigation, and asset scrutiny.

money.label: Financial consequence as proof of involvement
money.detail: Benefit or avoided testimony does not identify who caused a death.
